09 / 10

Limits and next validation

Current limits

  • Controlled phrase matching, with no trained model or LLM
  • PDF only, with manual skill entry as fallback
  • Invitation issuance has no staff UI
  • No interview scheduler or email notifications
  • No real-project suitability or time-saved study

Next validation

A mentor labels skills and shortlist suitability for a held-out set.

A project lead compares manual staffing with the prototype in a timed shadow review.

Measure precision, recall, Precision@3, missed suitable people and reviewer time before broader use.

1. SmartHireAI

Introduce the consultancy use case. The project supports internal bench consultants and external applicants. Describe spaCy phrase rules honestly as the extraction baseline.

2. The company brief

The original company DOCX lists these six core modules. All have implementations. Candidate registration is invitation-based. Staff invitation issuance has no UI yet. Source: docs/source/assignment.md, actual company DOCX, docs/manual/verification-2026-11-11.md.

3. A PLM staffing decision

Live demo: manager, Projects, 3DEXPERIENCE migration. Approve and lock v1. The displayed requirement is fictional. Source: docs/demo/script.md and apps/demo/management/commands/seed_demo.py. Screenshot is the recorded 9 November demo.

4. Coverage and Staffing fit

Show A's evidence drawer. Accepted project evidence earns 1.0. A confirmed form claim earns 0.5. Unknown and provisional matches earn zero. Credit counts each skill once. Source and exact calculation: docs/architecture/scoring.md sections 1, 2, 3 and 6.

5. The evidence path

No LLM reads instructions and assigns a score. The application performs actions through ordinary validated Django services. Hidden flags never subtract points or automatically reject a candidate. Sources: README.md, docs/architecture/scoring.md, ingestion and matching services.

6. The attacked resume

Upload fixtures/pdf/demo_candidate_b_attacked.pdf and open X-ray. Show the hidden migration text. Run matching and confirm B remains at 70. Source: docs/demo/script.md, tests/adversarial/test_attack_twins.py. The screenshot shows the prior recorded demo, not the final motion changes.

7. Correction and history

Upload demo_candidate_b_corrected.pdf. Accept Migration validation with a reason, rerun and show B at 100. Then open the earlier run at 70. Export the same shortlist filters. Sources: docs/demo/script.md, docs/architecture/scoring.md section 7.

8. Verification evidence

Do not describe the historical baseline as the latest final run. The submission audit adds fixes and checks. Use its actual result for a current count when presenting. Source: docs/manual/test-register.md, Summary and Metrics with denominators. Extraction quality and reviewer time are distinct from test pass rates.

9. Repository handover

The project uses Django templates with Bootstrap and HTMX, DRF for APIs, PostgreSQL for the assessed database and django-q2 for jobs. Secrets and private uploads stay out of the submitted source. README has both PowerShell and Git Bash setup. Sources: README.md, Makefile, pyproject.toml, requirements.in, docs/manual/submission-checklist.md.

10. Limits and next validation

Finish with a specific validation plan rather than claiming AI accuracy. Additional production work includes privacy review, retention/deletion, host isolation and shared throttling. The prototype demonstrates the six core modules and evidence controls. Sources: docs/manual/test-register.md Not measured, README.md Known limits, docs/manual/verification-2026-11-11.md. Do not promise a score-rule change.
